claims.text: The starting material is an equimolar CuMoTaWV refractory high-entropy-alloy film deposited by DC magnetron sputtering.
The as-deposited CuMoTaWV film is a nanocrystalline BCC solid solution.
The starting film has an average grain size of approximately 18 nm.
The film is initially deposited in an inert argon environment.
The proposed intervention is post-deposition annealing at approximately 300°C under a controlled low oxygen partial pressure.
Limited oxygen exposure during annealing will form a continuous nanometer-scale oxide layer on the alloy surface.
The proposed surface oxide is likely to contain CuO in a morphology favorable for lubrication.
Controlled oxidative annealing will improve grain-boundary adhesion.
Controlled oxidative annealing will smooth the film surface or alleviate its surface roughness.
The controlled oxide layer will act as a solid lubricant.
The oxide layer will reduce direct metal-to-metal contact during sliding.
Reduced direct contact and surface roughness will lower frictional dissipation, coefficient of friction, and wear.
Inert-annealed comparator films have a coefficient of friction of approximately 0.25 at room temperature.
Inert-annealed comparator films have a coefficient of friction of approximately 1.5 at 300°C.
Oxidative annealing will reduce the high-temperature coefficient of friction by more than 50%, toward a value below 1.0.
Oxidative annealing will reduce wear rate by approximately one order of magnitude relative to inert annealing.
The friction and wear benefit will persist from room temperature through at least 300°C.
The benefit requires oxygen partial pressure within a narrow optimal range and may fail above approximately 300°C because of excessive oxidation or phase degradation.
